### 12. Data Management Procedures

#### 12.1 General Principles

Data management activities at SGHRI are conducted in accordance with ICH E6(R2) and applicable Singapore regulations, including the Health Products Act and the Human Biomedical Research Act. The Data Manager, under the supervision of the Principal Investigator (PI), is responsible for ensuring that clinical data are recorded, processed, and maintained in a manner that preserves their accuracy, completeness, and reliability.

#### 12.2 Source Data

According to the staff list, the full_name of Alicia Wong is Alicia Wong. Record status: current.

Source data are defined as the original records of clinical findings, observations, or other activities necessary for the reconstruction and evaluation of the trial. Source data at SGHRI may include:

- Hospital medical records (electronic and paper).
- Participant diaries and questionnaires.
- Laboratory reports and diagnostic imaging reports.
- Pharmacy dispensing records.
- Case report forms (CRFs) completed by site staff.

The location of source data for each trial is documented in the Study Source Data Location List, which is maintained by the Data Manager and reviewed by the CRA during monitoring visits. Any changes to the source data location list must be approved by the PI and communicated to the Sponsor.

#### 12.3 Data Entry

Data entry into the EDC system is performed by the Clinical Research Coordinators and the Data Entry Clerk, where applicable. The following procedures apply:

- Data entry must be completed within 5 business days of the participant's visit, unless otherwise specified in the study-specific Data Management Plan.
- All data entries must be supported by source documents. Where the source document is not available at the time of entry, this must be flagged in the EDC system and resolved prior to the next monitoring visit.
- The Data Manager reviews the EDC system on a weekly basis to identify any missing or overdue data entries. The relevant CRC is notified by email, with a copy to the PI if the entry is more than 10 business days overdue.

#### 12.4 Query Management

Queries raised by the Sponsor, the CRA, or the Data Manager are processed as follows:

- Queries are logged in the EDC system and assigned to the responsible CRC or Data Manager.
- The responsible staff member must respond to the query within 5 business days, providing a clear resolution or a reasonable explanation for the discrepancy.
- The Data Manager reviews all query responses for consistency and completeness before they are submitted to the Sponsor.
- A query log is maintained for each trial and is available for review during monitoring visits and audits.

#### 14.2 Clinical Trial Services Agreement – Protocol SGH-ONC-024 (C-2024-001)

The contract specifies the name of Clinical Research Organization Asia Pacific as Clinical Research
Organization Asia Pacific. This is the current and operative legal name of the organisation as
stated in the agreement and as registered with the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority
(ACRA) of Singapore. The agreement covers the provision of clinical research organisation services
for Protocol SGH-ONC-024, including project management, monitoring, data management, safety
reporting, and regulatory support.

Key terms of the agreement include:

- **Scope of Services:** The CRO shall provide the services described in the Statement of Work
  (SOW) attached as Schedule A, including but not limited to site selection support, initiation,
  routine monitoring, close-out activities, and coordination of central laboratory services.
- **Term:** The agreement is effective from 15 January 2024 and shall remain in force until 14
  January 2026, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause 12.
- **Fees and Payment:** Fees are specified in Schedule B. Invoices shall be submitted monthly and
  are payable within 30 days of receipt.
- **Confidentiality:** Both parties agree to maintain the confidentiality of all protocol-related
  information and participant data in accordance with Clause 8.
- **Insurance and Indemnity:** The CRO shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less
  than SGD 2,000,000 per claim, as specified in Clause 10.

Amendments to this agreement are documented in the Amendment Log (Appendix 14.2). Any amendment
requires written approval from both the Site Director and the CRO's authorised signatory.

The contract specifies the name of Clinical Research Organization Asia Pacific as Clinical Research Organization Asia Pacific. Record status: current.

#### 14.3 Master Service Agreement – Central Laboratory Services (C-2023-089)

This agreement covers the provision of central laboratory services, including sample collection
kits, courier logistics, and laboratory testing for haematology, biochemistry, and biomarkers.
Pacific Diagnostics Pte Ltd is the contracted central laboratory for all protocols listed in the
SGHRI Master Protocol List.

#### 14.4 Site Support Agreement – Oncology Phase I Studies (C-2023-076)

This agreement outlines the support to be provided by Clinical Research Organization Asia Pacific
for the conduct of Phase I oncology studies at SGHRI. Support includes the assignment of a
dedicated Clinical Research Associate, provision of medical monitoring services, and coordination
of protocol-specific training for site staff.

---

### 15. EXTERNAL VENDORS AND SERVICE PROVIDERS

SGHRI engages a number of external vendors to support the conduct of clinical trials. The list
below reflects current vendor relationships as of the effective date of this document. Vendor
qualification records, including audits and performance evaluations, are maintained in the Vendor
Qualification File (Section 16).
### 16. VENDOR QUALIFICATION FILE

The Vendor Qualification File contains the following for each external vendor listed in Section 15:

- Vendor qualification questionnaires and risk assessments
- Site visit reports and audit findings
- Certificates of analysis and quality certifications
- Performance evaluation records, reviewed annually
- Insurance certificates and business registration documents
- Business continuity and disaster recovery plans

Vendor qualification is conducted prior to the first engagement and re-evaluated at least once every 24 months, or upon any significant change in vendor ownership, key personnel, or service scope. The Vendor Qualification File is maintained by the Site Director's office and is available for inspection upon request by the Sponsor, CRO, or Regulatory Authority.

#### 16.1 Vendor Performance Monitoring

Vendor performance is monitored through key performance indicators (KPIs) agreed upon at contract signing. KPIs include:

- Turnaround time for laboratory results
- Deviation and error rates
- Response time for query resolution
- Compliance with temperature monitoring and excursion reporting
- Courier pick-up and delivery reliability

Quarterly performance reviews are conducted by the Site Director, and any unresolved issues are escalated to the Vendor Management Committee. The current status of each vendor is indicated in the Vendor Status Log (Appendix 16.1). As of the effective date of this document, the status of Pacific Diagnostics Pte Ltd is current, and the status of Clinical Research Organization Asia Pacific is current.

### 17. SITE FACILITIES

SGHRI is located at 10 Research Link, Singapore 117604, within the Singapore Health Sciences Campus. The site occupies Levels 3 through 6 of the Research Tower.

#### 17.1 Physical Layout

- **Level 3 – Clinical Research Unit:** 12 examination rooms, 4 treatment bays, 2 procedure rooms, and a dedicated specimen collection area.
- **Level 4 – Laboratory and Sample Processing:** Sample reception, processing laboratory, and a -20°C and -80°C storage facility.
- **Level 5 – Administrative and Data Management:** Offices for the Site Director, Data Management, Regulatory Affairs, and the Monitoring Room.
- **Level 6 – Pharmacy and Investigational Product Storage:** Temperature-controlled storage rooms, a compounding area, and a secure dispensary.

#### 17.2 Access Control and Security

- Access to Levels 3–6 is controlled by electronic key cards. Card access is granted by the Facilities Office based on an individual's role and training records.
- The pharmacy and IP storage area on Level 6 has a separate keypad access system and a restricted access list maintained by the Principal Investigator.
- Laboratory areas are restricted to authorised laboratory personnel only.
- Visitor access is logged in the Visitor Register, and visitors must be accompanied by a staff member at all times.
- After-hours access requires prior approval from the Site Director or the on-call manager.

#### 17.3 Environmental Monitoring

- Temperature and humidity are monitored continuously in the IP storage, laboratory, and specimen storage areas.
- Monitoring systems are connected to a central alarm that alerts the Facilities Office and the on-call staff 24/7.
- Temperature excursion logs are maintained in the Quality Management System, and excursions are reported to the Sponsor within 24 hours if they affect investigational product or critical samples.
- Calibration of temperature probes and monitoring equipment is performed annually by an accredited external vendor.

### 18. EQUIPMENT CALIBRATION AND MAINTENANCE

All equipment used in the conduct of clinical trials is listed in the Equipment Inventory Log (Appendix 18.1). Each item is assigned a unique equipment ID and is subject to a scheduled calibration and maintenance program.

#### 18.1 Equipment Categories

- Centrifuges, refrigerators, freezers, and temperature data loggers
- Scales and balances
- Pipettes and volumetric equipment
- Blood pressure monitors, ECG machines, and other diagnostic devices
- Emergency equipment, including defibrillators and emergency carts

### 19. STAFF TRAINING AND QUALIFICATIONS

#### 19.1 Training Requirements

All staff involved in clinical trial activities must complete the following training prior to performing trial-related duties:

- Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training, with a refresher course every three years
- Human subjects protection training
- Site-specific training on trial protocols and procedures
- Training on the use of the electronic data capture (EDC) system
- Training on applicable SOPs

Training records are maintained in the Staff Training File (Appendix 19.1). Each staff member's training is documented with the date of completion, the trainer's name, and the validity period where applicable.

### 20. QUALITY ASSURANCE AND CONTROL

#### 20.1 Internal Quality Assurance

The site conducts periodic internal audits to ensure compliance with the protocol, GCP, and applicable regulations. Internal audits are performed by the Quality Assurance Officer, who is independent of the trial team.

Internal audit findings are documented in the Quality Management System. Corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) are tracked to closure, and the Sponsor is informed of any significant findings.

#### 20.2 External Quality Assurance

The site is subject to audits and inspections by the Sponsor, the CRO, and regulatory authorities. All audit and inspection reports are maintained in the Site Master File.

#### 20.3 Quality Indicators

The following quality indicators are monitored on a quarterly basis:

- Protocol deviation rates
- Data entry error rates
- Timeliness of safety reporting
- Compliance with informed consent procedures
- Visit completion rates

Any adverse trend in these indicators is investigated, and appropriate corrective actions are implemented.

**Site Master File – Singapore General Health Research Institute**

**Document ID:** SMF-2210-3.2
**Effective Date:** 01 May 2024
**Version:** 3.2
**Supersedes:** Version 3.1 (dated 01 Nov 2023)
**Site Code:** 2210

---

**1. Site Identification**

1.1 The Site Master File records the site_name as Singapore General Health Research Institute. Record status: current. This is the official, current legal and operating name of the clinical trial site and shall be used in all regulatory submissions, contracts, and correspondence with the Health Sciences Authority (HSA), the Domain Specific Review Board (DSRB), and all sponsors and Contract Research Organizations (CROs).

1.2 The site is located at 20 College Road, Singapore 169856. The physical facility comprises two connected blocks (Block A and Block B) on Levels 3 through 8, with the Clinical Trials Unit occupying the entirety of Level 4.

1.3 Site contact details:
- Principal Investigator: Dr. Mei Ling Tan (MBBS, MRCP)
- Site Director of Research Operations: Mr. Karthik Rajan
- Regulatory Affairs Manager: Ms. Priya Nair
- Quality Assurance Manager: Ms. Grace Koh
- Main line: +65 6321 4000
- Clinical Trials Unit direct: +65 6321 4777

---

**2. Purpose and Scope of this Document**

2.1 This Site Master File (SMF) serves as the central repository of site regulatory and administrative documents. It provides a comprehensive overview of the site's organisation, facilities, staff qualifications, standard operating procedures, and emergency preparedness to facilitate GCP-compliant conduct of clinical trials.

2.2 This document is intended for use by regulatory authorities, sponsors, CROs, and internal audit teams during site qualification visits, initiation visits, routine monitoring, and inspections.

2.3 The SMF is version-controlled. Any amendments require the approval of the Quality Assurance Manager and the Principal Investigator. A full revision history is maintained in Appendix A.

---

**3. Site Organisation and Governance**

3.1 The Singapore General Health Research Institute operates under the governance framework of the Singapore General Hospital (SGH) Campus, but functions as an independent research entity with its own Institutional Review Board oversight via DSRB.

3.2 The organisational hierarchy for clinical trial operations is as follows:
- **Principal Investigator (PI):** Dr. Mei Ling Tan – Overall responsibility for conduct of trials at the site.
- **Sub-Investigators:** Dr. Jason Wong, Dr. Farah Ismail, Dr. Benjamin Lee.
- **Clinical Research Coordinators (CRCs):** Ms. Siti Aminah, Ms. Rachel Lim, Mr. Daniel Teo.
- **Data Manager:** Mr. Wei Cheng Goh.
- **Regulatory Affairs:** Ms. Priya Nair.
- **Pharmacy:** Ms. Hui Min Chua (Investigational Product Dispensing).
- **Laboratory:** Ms. Anita Desai (Central Lab Liaison).

3.3 Delegation of Authority Log (DOA Log) is maintained in the Trial Master File for each individual study. The DOA Log is signed by the PI and each delegated staff member, and is reviewed at every monitoring visit.

---

**4. Facilities and Equipment**

4.1 The Clinical Trials Unit occupies Level 4 of Block B and includes:
- 6 examination rooms
- 1 procedure room equipped for minor procedures
- 1 dedicated specimen processing laboratory
- 1 ECG room
- 1 pharmacy storage room with a temperature-controlled investigational product (IP) storage unit
- 4 interview/counselling rooms
- 1 archive room with fireproof cabinets
- 2 administrative offices

4.2 Temperature monitoring: All refrigerators, freezers, and ambient temperature storage areas are monitored 24/7 via a centralised alarm system. Temperature logs are reviewed weekly by the QA Manager. The system has a battery backup and an automatic notification alert to the on-call staff.

4.3 Calibration: The following equipment is calibrated according to the manufacturer's specifications and site SOP-SM-007:
- Centrifuges (annual)
- Refrigerators and freezers (temperature probes calibrated annually)
- Weighing scales (annual)
- Blood pressure monitors (annual)
- ECG machines (annual)

5.3 The Clinical Trials Unit operates under the following escalation pathway:
- **First-line queries** (day-to-day operational issues): Lead CRC Ms. Siti Aminah
- **Protocol-related queries**: Principal Investigator Dr. Mei Ling Tan

### 12. Data Management Procedures

#### 12.1 General Principles

Data management activities at SGHRI are conducted in accordance with ICH E6(R2) and applicable Singapore regulations, including the Health Products Act and the Human Biomedical Research Act. The Data Manager, under the supervision of the Principal Investigator (PI), is responsible for ensuring that clinical data are recorded, processed, and maintained in a manner that preserves their accuracy, completeness, and reliability.

#### 12.2 Source Data

According to the staff list, the full_name of Alicia Wong is Alicia Wong. Record status: current.

Source data are defined as the original records of clinical findings, observations, or other activities necessary for the reconstruction and evaluation of the trial. Source data at SGHRI may include:

- Hospital medical records (electronic and paper).
- Participant diaries and questionnaires.
- Laboratory reports and diagnostic imaging reports.
- Pharmacy dispensing records.
- Case report forms (CRFs) completed by site staff.

The location of source data for each trial is documented in the Study Source Data Location List, which is maintained by the Data Manager and reviewed by the CRA during monitoring visits. Any changes to the source data location list must be approved by the PI and communicated to the Sponsor.

#### 12.3 Data Entry

Data entry into the EDC system is performed by the Clinical Research Coordinators and the Data Entry Clerk, where applicable. The following procedures apply:

- Data entry must be completed within 5 business days of the participant's visit, unless otherwise specified in the study-specific Data Management Plan.
- All data entries must be supported by source documents. Where the source document is not available at the time of entry, this must be flagged in the EDC system and resolved prior to the next monitoring visit.
- The Data Manager reviews the EDC system on a weekly basis to identify any missing or overdue data entries. The relevant CRC is notified by email, with a copy to the PI if the entry is more than 10 business days overdue.

#### 12.4 Query Management

Queries raised by the Sponsor, the CRA, or the Data Manager are processed as follows:

- Queries are logged in the EDC system and assigned to the responsible CRC or Data Manager.
- The responsible staff member must respond to the query within 5 business days, providing a clear resolution or a reasonable explanation for the discrepancy.
- The Data Manager reviews all query responses for consistency and completeness before they are submitted to the Sponsor.
- A query log is maintained for each trial and is available for review during monitoring visits and audits.

#### 16.1 Vendor Performance Monitoring

Vendor performance is monitored through key performance indicators (KPIs) agreed upon at contract signing. KPIs include:

- Turnaround time for laboratory results
- Deviation and error rates
- Response time for query resolution
- Compliance with temperature monitoring and excursion reporting
- Courier pick-up and delivery reliability

Quarterly performance reviews are conducted by the Site Director, and any unresolved issues are escalated to the Vendor Management Committee. ### 17. SITE FACILITIES

SGHRI is located at 10 Research Link, Singapore 117604, within the Singapore Health Sciences Campus. The site occupies Levels 3 through 6 of the Research Tower.

#### 17.1 Physical Layout

- **Level 3 – Clinical Research Unit:** 12 examination rooms, 4 treatment bays, 2 procedure rooms, and a dedicated specimen collection area.
- **Level 4 – Laboratory and Sample Processing:** Sample reception, processing laboratory, and a -20°C and -80°C storage facility.
- **Level 5 – Administrative and Data Management:** Offices for the Site Director, Data Management, Regulatory Affairs, and the Monitoring Room.
- **Level 6 – Pharmacy and Investigational Product Storage:** Temperature-controlled storage rooms, a compounding area, and a secure dispensary.

#### 17.2 Access Control and Security

- Access to Levels 3–6 is controlled by electronic key cards. Card access is granted by the Facilities Office based on an individual's role and training records.
- The pharmacy and IP storage area on Level 6 has a separate keypad access system and a restricted access list maintained by the Principal Investigator.
- Laboratory areas are restricted to authorised laboratory personnel only.
- Visitor access is logged in the Visitor Register, and visitors must be accompanied by a staff member at all times.
- After-hours access requires prior approval from the Site Director or the on-call manager.

#### 17.3 Environmental Monitoring

- Temperature and humidity are monitored continuously in the IP storage, laboratory, and specimen storage areas.
- Monitoring systems are connected to a central alarm that alerts the Facilities Office and the on-call staff 24/7.
- Temperature excursion logs are maintained in the Quality Management System, and excursions are reported to the Sponsor within 24 hours if they affect investigational product or critical samples.
- Calibration of temperature probes and monitoring equipment is performed annually by an accredited external vendor.

Internal audit findings are documented in the Quality Management System. Corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) are tracked to closure, and the Sponsor is informed of any significant findings.

#### 20.2 External Quality Assurance

The site is subject to audits and inspections by the Sponsor, the CRO, and regulatory authorities. All audit and inspection reports are maintained in the Site Master File.

#### 20.3 Quality Indicators

The following quality indicators are monitored on a quarterly basis:

- Protocol deviation rates
- Data entry error rates
- Timeliness of safety reporting
- Compliance with informed consent procedures
- Visit completion rates

Any adverse trend in these indicators is investigated, and appropriate corrective actions are implemented.
